ARTICLES_LIST.TITLE: The importance of certifications in fire protection systems: Solicmex’s commitment to safety
ARTICLES_LIST.DESCRIPTION:
The importance of certifications in fire protection systems: Solicmex’s commitment to safety

In the field of engineering and fire protection, quality, reliability, and regulatory compliance are not optional—they are essential. At Solicmex, we understand that the safety of people, facilities, and assets depends directly on the proper implementation of systems certified and validated by nationally and internationally recognized standards.

For this reason, we comply with key standards such as NFPA 20, NFPA 25, FM Global, and NOM-002-STPS, which support our work in engineering, installation, maintenance, and repair of fire protection systems.

Why are certifications in fire protection important?

Certifications are not just technical documents: they represent a guarantee of quality, safety, and legal compliance. Working under certified standards ensures that fire protection systems:

  • Will function properly in critical situations
  • Meet legal and regulatory requirements
  • Protect human lives and physical assets
  • Reduce operational and financial risks

In short, a certified installation can make the difference between a controlled incident and a catastrophe.

Certifications and standards that support Solicmex

NFPA 20 – Fire pump systems

The National Fire Protection Association establishes in the NFPA 20 standard the guidelines for the installation of fire pumps.

This standard ensures that:

  • Pumps have the appropriate capacity for each type of risk
  • Systems operate reliably during emergencies
  • Installation meets international standards

At Solicmex, we apply NFPA 20 to ensure that each pumping system operates efficiently when it is needed most.

NFPA 25 – Inspection, testing, and maintenance

The NFPA 25 standard regulates the inspection, testing, and maintenance of fire protection systems.

Its importance lies in the fact that it:

  • Ensures systems are always operational
  • Detects failures before emergencies occur
  • Extends the lifespan of equipment

Solicmex implements maintenance programs based on NFPA 25, ensuring the operational continuity of installed systems.

FM Global – High-level industrial certification

FM Global is one of the most recognized organizations worldwide in risk assessment and industrial system certification.

Working under FM Global standards implies:

  • Highly reliable and proven designs
  • Risk reduction for insurers and companies
  • Compliance with international safety requirements

This certification is especially relevant in industrial projects, where the level of risk is higher.

NOM-002-STPS – Fire safety in Mexico

The Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare establishes NOM-002-STPS, which regulates safety conditions for fire prevention and protection in workplaces in Mexico.

This standard ensures:

  • Legal compliance within the national territory
  • Safe conditions for workers
  • Clear prevention and response protocols

At Solicmex, we ensure that every project complies with NOM-002-STPS, aligning safety with current Mexican regulations.

The added value of working with Solicmex

As stated in the company’s philosophy, Solicmex is a specialized and certified company in engineering, installation, maintenance, and repair of fire protection systems. This translates into:

  • Projects designed under international standards
  • Guaranteed regulatory compliance
  • Comprehensive solutions tailored to each client
  • Greater trust and support for companies and industries

ARTICLES_LIST.TITLE: What is NFPA and why is it important in fire protection systems?
ARTICLES_LIST.DESCRIPTION:
What is NFPA and why is it important in fire protection systems?

In the field of fire protection, safety depends on much more than equipment and technology. To ensure reliable, efficient systems capable of responding properly during an emergency, there are international standards and regulations that govern the design, installation, maintenance, and inspection of fire protection systems.

One of the most important and globally recognized organizations in this field is the NFPA (National Fire Protection Association), whose standards are used in thousands of industrial, commercial, and institutional projects around the world.

What is NFPA?

The NFPA, or National Fire Protection Association, is an international organization founded in 1896 in the United States, dedicated to developing standards and regulations related to fire prevention, fire protection, electrical safety, and risk management.

Today, NFPA standards are considered a global technical reference and are used in more than 100 countries to design safe and efficient fire protection systems.

The primary objective of NFPA is to reduce the risk of fires and other hazards through technical guidelines developed by engineers, manufacturers, authorities, and safety specialists.

Why is NFPA important in fire protection systems?

NFPA standards ensure that fire protection systems function properly when they are truly needed.

Without adequate technical standards, systems may experience critical failures during emergencies, putting human lives, infrastructure, and business operations at risk.

The importance of NFPA lies in establishing clear criteria to:

  • Design safe and efficient systems
  • Standardize installation processes
  • Ensure proper maintenance procedures
  • Reduce operational and financial risks
  • Protect human lives and property
  • Comply with legal and insurance requirements

Thanks to these standards, companies can rely on systems aligned with internationally recognized safety practices.

What do NFPA standards regulate?

NFPA standards cover virtually every component related to fire protection systems.

The main regulated areas include:

  • Automatic sprinkler systems
  • Fire pumps
  • Fire alarm and detection systems
  • Portable fire extinguishers
  • Fire protection piping networks
  • Clean agent suppression systems
  • Inspection and maintenance procedures
  • Electrical safety
  • Emergency signage and evacuation systems

Each standard is specifically designed to address different aspects of comprehensive fire protection.

Main NFPA standards used in fire protection systems

NFPA 13 – Automatic sprinkler systems

NFPA 13 regulates the design and installation of automatic sprinkler systems.

This standard establishes criteria related to:

  • Sprinkler coverage
  • Hazard classifications
  • Required flow rates and pressures
  • Spacing between devices
  • Piping materials and specifications

Proper implementation helps control or extinguish fires during their early stages.

NFPA 20 – Fire pumps

NFPA 20 regulates the installation of fire pumps, which are essential for supplying water at the proper pressure during emergencies.

The standard includes guidelines for:

  • Electric and diesel fire pumps
  • Jockey pumps
  • Power supply systems
  • Pump rooms
  • Performance testing

Proper installation according to NFPA 20 ensures operational reliability during critical situations.

NFPA 25 – Inspection, testing, and maintenance

NFPA 25 establishes procedures for the inspection, testing, and maintenance of fire protection systems.

Its purpose is to ensure that systems remain fully operational at all times.

The standard includes:

  • Fire pump testing
  • Valve inspections
  • Piping evaluations
  • Flow testing
  • Corrosion and leak detection

Maintenance programs based on NFPA 25 are essential to prevent failures during real emergencies.

NFPA 72 – Fire alarm and detection systems

NFPA 72 regulates fire alarm and detection systems.

This standard defines criteria related to:

  • Smoke and heat detectors
  • Control panels
  • Audible and visual notification devices
  • Manual pull stations
  • Remote monitoring systems

Early detection is critical to reducing damage and ensuring safe evacuation.

NFPA 10 – Portable fire extinguishers

NFPA 10 regulates the selection, installation, and inspection of portable fire extinguishers.

It includes criteria for:

  • Fire classifications
  • Types of extinguishing agents
  • Strategic placement
  • Maintenance and recharge procedures
  • Maximum travel distances

Portable extinguishers represent the first line of response against incipient fires.

NFPA and fire protection engineering

Today, fire protection engineering depends heavily on compliance with NFPA standards.

These standards allow the development of safe projects through:

  • Risk analysis
  • Hydraulic calculations
  • Fire network design
  • Proper equipment selection
  • Technical documentation and drawings
  • Evacuation planning strategies

As a result, systems can be properly adapted to different facilities and hazard levels.

Benefits of implementing NFPA-compliant systems

Implementing systems designed according to NFPA standards provides multiple benefits:

  • Improved life safety
  • Reduced property damage
  • Greater operational reliability
  • Regulatory compliance
  • Compatibility with insurance requirements
  • Reduced operational and financial risks

In industrial, commercial, and corporate sectors, working under NFPA standards is now considered essential.

NFPA standards in Mexico

Although NFPA is a U.S.-based organization, its standards are widely used in Mexico across industries, hospitals, hotels, shopping centers, corporate buildings, and manufacturing plants.

Additionally, many Mexican official standards reference NFPA technical criteria to ensure safe installations aligned with international safety standards.

The importance of working with certified specialists

Designing, installing, and maintaining fire protection systems requires technical expertise, experience, and regulatory compliance.

A specialized company should have:

  • Certified and trained personnel
  • Knowledge of NFPA standards
  • Experience in fire protection engineering
  • Inspection and maintenance capabilities
  • Proper equipment and technology

Working with specialists ensures reliable systems prepared to respond effectively during emergencies.

Conclusion

NFPA represents one of the most important pillars of fire safety worldwide.

Its standards enable the development of reliable systems capable of protecting human lives, infrastructure, and critical operations through internationally recognized technical requirements.

Beyond regulatory compliance, implementing NFPA-compliant systems is an investment in safety, operational continuity, and risk reduction for any modern company or institution.

ARTICLES_LIST.TITLE: What Is a Fire Protection System? Importance, Operation, and Essential Components
ARTICLES_LIST.DESCRIPTION:
What Is a Fire Protection System?

Fire protection is one of the most important aspects of safety in industrial, commercial, residential, and institutional facilities. A fire can endanger human lives, cause major financial losses, and severely impact business continuity. For this reason, fire protection systems have become an essential part of modern engineering and industrial safety.

A fire protection system is a combination of equipment, devices, and technologies designed to detect, alert, control, and extinguish fires either automatically or manually. Its primary objective is to minimize damage, protect people, and preserve buildings, machinery, and critical assets.


How Does a Fire Protection System Work?

The operation of a fire protection system depends on the type of protection implemented, but it generally follows a sequence of detection, alarm, and suppression. When a detector identifies smoke, heat, or fire, the system activates audible and visual alarms and, depending on the configuration, may automatically activate sprinklers, pumping systems, or suppression agents.

Automatic systems are designed to control fires in their early stages, preventing their spread and allowing safe evacuation while emergency responders arrive.


Main Components of a Fire Protection System

Fire protection systems are composed of several specialized elements that work together to ensure effective protection.


1. Fire Detection and Alarm Systems

These systems quickly identify signs of fire through smoke, heat, or flame detectors. Once an emergency is detected, audible and visual alarms are activated to alert building occupants.

Main components include:

  • Smoke detectors
  • Heat detectors
  • Control panels
  • Sirens and strobes
  • Manual pull stations
  • Monitoring modules

2. Automatic Sprinkler Systems

Automatic sprinkler systems are one of the most effective methods for controlling fires. They operate through pressurized piping connected to thermally sensitive sprinklers that activate automatically when high temperatures are detected.

There are several types of sprinkler systems:

  • Wet pipe systems
  • Dry pipe systems
  • Pre-action systems
  • Deluge systems

3. Fire Pump Systems

The fire pump room is responsible for providing the pressure and flow required to supply hydraulic fire protection systems. It includes main pumps, jockey pumps, controllers, valves, and backup systems.


4. Hydrant and Hose Systems

Hydrant systems allow manual firefighting through hoses and special connections used by internal brigades or fire departments.


5. Special Fire Suppression Systems

Some environments require alternatives to water-based suppression systems. In these cases, specialized suppression systems are used, such as:

  • Clean agent systems
  • CO₂ systems
  • Foam systems
  • Commercial kitchen fire suppression systems

The Importance of Fire Protection Engineering

Designing a fire protection system requires specialized knowledge in hydraulics, international standards, industrial safety, and risk analysis. Each project must be tailored to the specific characteristics of the facility and comply with technical standards such as NFPA 13, NFPA 20, NFPA 25, and NFPA 72.

Proper engineering ensures that systems operate correctly during emergencies and comply with legal and operational requirements.


Fire Protection System Maintenance

A fire protection system requires periodic inspections, testing, and maintenance to ensure proper operation. Maintenance activities include valve inspections, pump testing, alarm inspections, detector cleaning, and hydraulic testing.

Preventive maintenance is essential to guarantee system reliability during real emergency situations.


Benefits of Having a Fire Protection System

  • Protection of human lives
  • Reduction of property damage
  • Business continuity
  • Regulatory compliance
  • Reduced financial risks
  • Improved safety for employees and visitors

Solicmex Commitment to Safety

At Solicmex, we specialize in the engineering, installation, maintenance, and repair of fire protection systems. Our mission is to provide comprehensive, efficient, and reliable solutions that ensure the safety of every project.

We work under international standards and with highly trained personnel to develop systems tailored to each client’s specific needs, ensuring quality, regulatory compliance, and maximum protection.
